items.title: [Twisted] Twisted: Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service in the Twisted HTTP/2 Server via Rapid Stream Reset
items.summary: SummaryAn uncontrolled-resource-consumption vulnerability (CWE-400) in the Twisted HTTP/2 server lets any unauthenticated remote client exhaust server CPU over a single connection. A client that sends a request header block with END_STREAM and then immediately resets the stream makes the server route and render the request before it processes the reset. Reset streams are freed and never count against the concurrent-stream limit, and no reset-rate limiter exists, so the pattern can be repeated at line rate on one connection. This is the HTTP/2 Rapid Reset class, CVE-2023-44487.DetailsFor one received segment the h2 events are processed in order in H2Connection.dataReceived. A HEADERS(END_STREAM) followed by RST_STREAM yields RequestReceived, StreamEnded, then StreamReset, so the request is dispatched and rendered on stream end before the reset is handled:# src/twisted/web/_http2.py  (H2Connection.dataReceived)for event in events:    if isinstance(event, h2.events.RequestReceived):        self._requestReceived(event)     # allocate the request    elif isinstance(event, h2.events.StreamEnded):        self._requestEnded(event)        # -> requestComplete -> render() synchronously    elif isinstance(event, h2.events.StreamReset):        self._requestAborted(event)      # processed last, frees the stream_requestAborted frees the reset stream, so it never occupies the 100-stream concurrency budget, and nothing in _http2.py counts or throttles opened-and-reset streams. The 2019 flood fix (GHSA-32gv) bounds outbound control-frame buffering only and does not apply to this path.Affected product: Twisted, twisted.web HTTP/2 serverAffected versions: confirmed against 26.4.0PoCOn any Twisted HTTP/2 endpoint, open one connection and, in a tight loop, send a HEADERS frame with END_STREAM on a fresh stream identifier immediately followed by a RST_STREAM for that stream, at line rate. No credentials are required. The server renders each request on stream end before the reset frees the stream, and a freed stream never counts toward the concurrent-stream limit, so the loop is never throttled.Because every cancelled stream is still dispatched in full and reset streams do not accumulate, the connection is never throttled or closed, so the forced work grows with the number of pairs sent. Sustained on one connection this saturates a CPU core under only a trickle of traffic, whereas a client that instead leaves its streams open is closed once it reaches the concurrent-stream limit.ImpactThis is an unauthenticated remote denial of service (CWE-400, CWE-770) by CPU exhaustion. One connection forces unbounded request rendering at a few frames per cancelled request, bypassing the concurrent-stream limit. It is the HTTP/2 Rapid Reset class (CVE-2023-44487), not covered by the earlier Twisted flood fix, with no confidentiality or integrity impact and no code execution.Referenceshttps://github.com/twisted/twisted/security/advisories/GHSA-vpp8-g58w-m8mphttps://github.com/twisted/twisted/pull/12749https://github.com/twisted/twisted/commit/498939422b69d5a75c4b8f81fa7926423dac534dhttps://github.com/twisted/twisted/releases/tag/twisted-26.10.0rc1https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2023-44487https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vpp8-g58w-m8mp

items.title: [praisonai] PraisonAI vulnerable to Remote Code Execution via Broken AST Sandbox
items.summary: SummaryJobWorkflowExecutor._exec_inline_python() is designed to safely execute inline Python expressions from YAML workflow script: steps using AST validation. The function claims to block dangerous operations by (a) checking all AST nodes against an allowlist, and (b) providing a builtins whitelist that omits import, exec, eval, and open.The sandbox is broken. The module import allowlist (allowed_modules) explicitly includes 'os', and the AST allowlist permits ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom, ast.Call, and ast.Attribute nodes. This means the following malicious workflow script: step passes all AST validation checks and executes without error.Attack ScenarioAttacker creates or contributes a YAML workflow file (type: job) with a script: step containing import os; os.system(...).A user or CI pipeline with PRAISONAI_ALLOW_JOB_WORKFLOWS=true executes the workflow via praisonai workflow run malicious.yaml.Arbitrary OS commands execute with the privileges of the calling process.This is particularly dangerous in multi-tenant or CI environments where YAML workflows may originate from untrusted sources (e.g., downloaded templates, shared repositories, AI-generated workflows).PoCComplete instructions, including specific configuration details, to reproduce the vulnerability.ImpactRoot Cause — Lines 364–372:pythonallowed_modules = {'os', 'datetime', 'time', 'json', 'math', 're', 'collections', 'itertools'}if isinstance(node, ast.Import):    for alias in node.names:        if alias.name.split('.')[0] not in allowed_modules:            return {"ok": False, "error": f"Import of '{alias.name}' not allowed..."}os is trusted because it is commonly used for path operations (os.path, os.getcwd). However, os.system(), os.popen(), os.execvp(), os.spawn*(), and os._exit() are all accessible once the module is imported, none of which are individually blocked.The builtins restriction (blocking import) is irrelevant because the code uses a real import statement processed by the Python bytecode compiler — not a import() call.Proof-of-Concept validation (static — no remote network call made):pythonimport ast_ALLOWED_NODES = (    ast.Expression, ast.BoolOp, ast.BinOp, ast.UnaryOp, ast.Compare,    ast.IfExp, ast.Constant, ast.Name, ast.Load, ast.Store, ast.Subscript,    ast.List, ast.Tuple, ast.Dict, ast.Set,    ast.And, ast.Or, ast.Not, ast.Eq, ast.NotEq, ast.Lt, ast.LtE,    ast.Gt, ast.GtE, ast.In, ast.NotIn, ast.Add, ast.Sub, ast.Mult,    ast.Div, ast.Mod, ast.FloorDiv, ast.USub, ast.UAdd,    ast.Call, ast.Attribute, ast.keyword, ast.Starred,    ast.Module, ast.Assign, ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom, ast.alias,)allowed_modules = {'os', 'datetime', 'time', 'json', 'math', 're', 'collections', 'itertools'}malicious = "import os\nresult = os.system('id')"tree = ast.parse(malicious, mode="exec")all_pass = Truefor node in ast.walk(tree):    if not isinstance(node, _ALLOWED_NODES):        print(f"BLOCKED: {type(node).name}")        all_pass = False    if isinstance(node, ast.Import):        for alias in node.names:            if alias.name.split('.')[0] not in allowed_modules:                print(f"IMPORT BLOCKED: {alias.name}")                all_pass = Falseprint("SANDBOX BYPASSED" if all_pass else "sandbox holds")Output: SANDBOX BYPASSEDRecommended FixRemove 'os' from allowed_modules and replace it with only the safe submodule: 'os.path'. Then validate that the imported name is specifically os.path, not os:python# BEFORE (vulnerable)allowed_modules = {'os', 'datetime', 'time', 'json', 'math', 're', 'collections', 'itertools'}AFTER (safe)allowed_modules = {'datetime', 'time', 'json', 'math', 're', 'collections', 'itertools', 'pathlib'}If os.path is needed, handle it explicitly:if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):    if node.module == 'os.path':        pass  # allow 'from os.path import join, exists' only    elif node.module and node.module.split('.')[0] not in allowed_modules:        return {"ok": False, "error": f"Import of '{node.module}' not allowed."}Additionally, block ast.Import of os entirely, and consider also removing re (which can be used for ReDoS/CPU exhaustion) and collections (which can be used to reach subclasses-style gadgets).Referenceshttps://github.com/MervinPraison/PraisonAI/security/advisories/GHSA-26mh-57q7-jfvrhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-61438https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-62248https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/praisonai-before-remote-code-execution-via-broken-ast-sandboxhttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-26mh-57q7-jfvr
